gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-lao: Neon's line never changes width, like stamped metal. Noto Sans Lao is the foil: a plain sans with a lofty x-height and mouths left wide open, built for running text where Neon is built to be looked at.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Neon glows with one unbroken line width, every letter spaced out and tall in the lowercase. Noto Sans Lydian is a plain sans with capitals barely above its lowercase; try it smaller.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-modi: Glowing signage on top, open daylight below. Neon is at its best as a shouting display face with one thickness throughout, while Noto Sans Modi does its work quietly, its low capital-to-lowercase contrast and open curves.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-multani: Vibrant and buzzing, then suddenly quiet. Noto Sans Multani takes over where Neon stops: Neon commands attention with full-width stroke joins, while the sans below it keeps a lofty x-height and an e with a wide gap.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-newa: Modern in feel, Noto Sans Newa has a clearly open lowercase e. Noto Sans Newa carries long stretches with tall counters and bowls, while Neon above it hums in a flat gray of constant line weight, glowing and loud.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-old-permic: Friendly rounded forms, open to the side, make this body feel easy. Neon is best at loud, single-width display lettering, whereas Noto Sans Old Permic does its job with lowercase that nearly matches the capitals in height.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-noto-sans-old-sogdian: Neon draws a t whose crossbar and stem share one width, glowing and vibrant. Noto Sans Old Sogdian follows with a tall x-height nearly reaching cap height, so the two feel crisp together even shrunk down.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-pathway-extreme: Marker-nib glow meets tidy rounds. The strongest quality is the gap between Neon's directionless, one-width line and Pathway Extreme, a sans-serif with clear openings, stubby ascenders and descenders, and a big x-height.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-radio-canada: Neon buzzes while Radio Canada stays level. Neon does its best work glowing at display size with open spacing, while Radio Canada, a sans with tall full c, s and z, holds a steady line with clear curve endings.
gen-dafont-neon-gf-sono: Neon-bright on top, easygoing below. Its strongest quality is true monoline drawing, which Sono answers in a sans with tall lowercase, wide default spacing and each a left ajar.
